clue.text: Famished gunners love having goddess round

parts.note: the Royal Artillery, the army's gunners

indicators.note: the goddess's name goes round the zero, enclosing it

parts.note: Venus, Roman goddess of love
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Hungry artillerymen adore a goddess who is coming round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravenous means extremely hungry, a close synonym of famished.

clue.text: Curse Mike cutting several articles

indicators.note: Mike cuts into the run of articles, splitting it

parts.note: the articles AN, A, THE and A strung together
M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone swears as a man named Mike slices through a pile of newspaper articles.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is a formal ecclesiastical curse or something cursed and detested.

clue.text: Sound off about Republican, one living abroad

indicators.note: the word for sounding off goes about, enclosing, the Republican's letter

parts.note: to expatiate is to speak or write at great length, to sound off

explanation.surface: A Republican living overseas is sounding off about his party.
explanation.definitionFit: An expatriate is a person who lives outside their native country.

clue.text: Give too much publicity to do with former model

parts.note: over can mean concerning, to do with, as in a row over money
ex means former, as in ex-wife
to model is to pose for an artist

explanation.surface: Publicity about a former model gets too much exposure.
explanation.definitionFit: To overexpose someone is to give them more media attention than is good for them.

clue.text: Distant rooftops maybe arranged like New York's?

indicators.note: the letters are arranged into a new order

parts.note: NY is New York, with the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: Far-off roofs laid out in the manner of Manhattan's famous outline.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the surface itself describes the answer: New York's skyline is the most famous of all.
explanation.definitionFit: A skyline is the outline of buildings seen against the sky from afar, of which distant rooftops are an example.

clue.text: Loyal Brussels right back

indicators.note: in a down clue, back means the letters run upwards, read in reverse order

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the EU, the European Union

explanation.surface: A faithful Brussels full-back playing on the right side of defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right back' looks like a football position, but 'back' is a reversal signal acting on the two pieces before it.
explanation.definitionFit: True means faithful and steadfast, as in a true friend.

clue.text: Drivers leaving odd bric-a-brac for baker's agent

indicators.note: odd means peculiar, so the letters of bric-a-brac are jumbled
the motoring club's letters leave the jumble, taken out of it

parts.note: the RAC, the Royal Automobile Club, is a British motoring organisation for drivers

explanation.surface: Motorists abandon some strange junk, leaving behind a baker's raising agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' tempts a solver to take alternate letters of bric-a-brac; that gives no word, and it is an anagram signal instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Bicarb, short for bicarbonate of soda, is the raising agent bakers use to make dough rise.

clue.text: Men only put in reduced bid behind the scenes

indicators.note: the men-only word is put inside the shortened bid
the bid is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: an offer is a bid
a stag party or stag night is for men only

explanation.surface: A men-only group makes a lowered offer for something.
explanation.definitionFit: Offstage describes what happens out of the audience's sight, behind the scenery of a theatre.

clue.text: King and queen cook, securing India's top cover

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina

indicators.note: the cook holds on to the letter, securing it inside

parts.note: a chef is a cook

indicators.note: top means the first letter of the word

parts.note: the word India, whose first letter is wanted

explanation.surface: A royal couple and their cook handle the best of India's produce.
explanation.definitionFit: A kerchief is a square of cloth worn to cover the head or neck.

clue.text: A good sleuth probes Middle East collector

indicators.note: the pieces probe, entering inside, the Middle East abbreviation

parts.note: a PI is a private investigator, a sleuth

explanation.surface: A good private detective investigates a hoarder in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: A magpie is a person who obsessively collects things, after the bird's reputation for taking shiny objects.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is famed for hoarding bright trinkets, so the name is given to a compulsive collector.

clue.text: A peer films erratic guides having their ups and downs

definitions.text: guides having their ups and downs

indicators.note: erratic means irregular and wandering, so the letters move about

explanation.surface: A nobleman shoots shaky footage of tour guides whose fortunes rise and fall.
explanation.walkthrough: The ups and downs are hills and valleys, not changing fortunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief maps show terrain in raised form or shading, guiding the reader through hills and valleys.

clue.text: Compiler's avoiding Times forecaster

indicators.note: the two letters for times are avoided, removed from the setter

parts.note: a crossword compiler is a setter
times is the multiplication sign X, but here T for time, twice

explanation.surface: The puzzle setter of The Times claims to see the future, steering clear of the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T makes Times look like the newspaper this puzzle appears in; it stands for two Ts, T being the abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: A seer is a prophet, one who sees and foretells the future.

clue.text: One's in a phonebox, somehow rejecting foreign callers?

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the noun: the rejection of foreigners

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone shut in a telephone box refuses to take calls from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The callers are visitors from abroad, not telephone callers.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenophobia is the fear or dislike of foreigners, shown by turning away visitors from other countries.

clue.text: Chief instigator putting pressure on banker about note

indicators.note: in a down clue the pressure letter sits on top of the rest

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

indicators.note: the river goes about, around, the note

parts.note: a river has banks, so it is a banker
a memo is a note

explanation.surface: The ringleader is pressuring a banking man over a written note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is a crossword joke: a river is something with banks.
explanation.definitionFit: A prime mover is the person who initiates and drives something, its leading instigator.

clue.text: At one time eating hot food mainly in church event

indicators.note: the word for formerly eats, swallows, the rest

parts.note: once means at one time, formerly

indicators.note: the shortened curry goes in the church letters

parts.note: CE, the Church of England

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a curry is spicy hot food

explanation.surface: Formerly, having a curry in church was quite a happening.
explanation.definitionFit: An occurrence is an incident or happening, a synonym of event.

clue.text: Soldiers circle large fungus

parts.note: paras are paratroopers
a circle is the letter O

explanation.surface: Troops form a ring around a big mushroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The parasol is a tall edible mushroom with a broad umbrella-like cap.
explanation.definitionFit: The parasol mushroom is a fungus named for its cap, which opens like a sunshade.

clue.text: One of many featuring in Victoria's policy

definitions.text: One of many featuring in Victoria
definitions.meaning: London's Victoria railway station has many numbered ...
a party's ... is its set of declared policies

explanation.walkthrough: Victoria looks like a queen or a politician whose policy is in question; it is the London rail terminus, full of platforms.
explanation.definitionFit: A station has many platforms where trains stop, and a political platform is a stated programme of aims.

clue.text: In fury, business group withdraws guard for lights, etc?

indicators.note: the reversed group sits in the word for fury

parts.note: rage is fury

indicators.note: withdraws means draws back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the CBI, the Confederation of British Industry

explanation.surface: An industry lobby furiously pulls its security guards from street lighting.
explanation.walkthrough: Lights are lungs, an old butcher's word for animal lungs, so the guard is the bony cage protecting them and the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The ribs form a protective cage around the lungs and heart, guarding the vital organs.

clue.text: Successful student King George left out of praise

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, King George

indicators.note: the letter for left is taken out of the word for praise

parts.note: to adulate is to praise excessively

explanation.surface: A star pupil leaves after the king offers no praise.
explanation.definitionFit: A graduate has successfully completed a degree course, the student who passed.

clue.text: It's worn by drivers about to stop lady

indicators.note: about is put in to stop, plug, the lady

parts.note: madam is a polite form of address for a lady
ca, circa, means about

explanation.surface: Something worn by motorists, about to halt a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn' suggests clothing like driving gloves; it means worn down by wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: Macadam is a road surface of compacted stones, worn away by the traffic that drives over it.

clue.text: Wally always got stuck into state, solemnly

parts.note: a wally is British slang for a fool, an ass
ever means always, as in ever hopeful
to get stuck into food is to eat it heartily, so ate

explanation.surface: The fool, as always, got bogged down in the matter of state.
explanation.walkthrough: A wally is British slang for a silly person.
explanation.definitionFit: To asseverate is to declare earnestly and emphatically, a formal word for a solemn statement.

clue.text: Pace kept by strongest riders

indicators.note: the letters are kept, held inside, by the two words that follow

parts.note: the answer runs across the join of these two words, from the end of the first into the start of the second

explanation.surface: The best cyclists or jockeys set the speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A stride is a single long step, the measure of a walker's or runner's pace.

clue.text: Revolutionary place to hide bread overseas

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a lair is an animal's hiding place

explanation.surface: A rebel hides a loaf somewhere abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money; the rial is the currency of Iran, Oman and Yemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, and the rial is a currency used in several Middle Eastern countries.

clue.text: Painter of unusual old instrument once

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: O for old, as in OT, Old Testament

explanation.surface: An artist owns a strange antique instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The fortepiano was the early form of the piano, used in the eighteenth century and later superseded.

clue.text: Smell bad second portion of game

definitions.meaning: the second half of ping-..., the game of table tennis

explanation.walkthrough: Pong is British slang for a bad smell or to give one off.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to stink, and the word also completes the name ping-pong for table tennis.

clue.text: Museum initially lambasting hooligan

parts.note: the V and A, the Victoria and Albert Museum in London

indicators.note: initially means the first letter only of the following word

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A London museum is slamming a yob who damaged its collection.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A is London's Victoria and Albert Museum of art and design.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal is someone who wilfully destroys property, a hooligan.

clue.text: Forest dweller's attack interrupting summer in retreat

indicators.note: the attack word breaks into the reversed adder
retreating means going backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a summer is one who sums, an adder
to pan is to criticise harshly, to attack

explanation.surface: An animal in the woods is set upon during a summer retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer' is the season to the eye, but here it is one who adds up.
explanation.definitionFit: The red panda is a small reddish mammal living in the mountain forests of the Himalayas and China.

clue.text: One makes a killing backing winning horse on entering

indicators.note: backing means the whole is read in reverse
the word for on enters the horse's name

parts.note: Red Rum, who won the Grand National three times
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: A punter cleans up by backing a winner on course.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Rum is the famous British racehorse that won the Grand National steeplechase three times in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: A killer is someone who commits murder; the definition plays on making a killing as making a fortune.
